ui.a11y.p1: CropLytics is built to work with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone in bright sun and without colour. Here is what is supported and how we checked it.
ui.a11y.s1: (Menu): type about 15% larger, bold dark ink, no light greys. All text meets WCAG AA, and body text meets AAA in this mode. Remembered on this device.
ui.a11y.s2: (Menu): stops the ten-year replay, the rain animation, fly-ins and transitions. The device setting "reduce motion" is honoured everywhere as well.
ui.a11y.s3: every step, panel, map button (zoom in, zoom out, tilt, reset north, play and pause, layers) and dialog works with Tab, Enter, Space and the arrow keys. Escape closes dialogs and pop-ups. A "Skip to field panel" link is the first stop.
ui.a11y.s4: the "List" button shows every field, farm and nearby reserve as a list with name, crop, acres and region, so the map is never required.
ui.a11y.s5: type an address, a place name or "lat, lon" to open that spot.
ui.a11y.s6: field access reads "✓ OK", "~ Marginal", "✕ Too wet"; crop groups use a colour-blind-safe palette with a letter; charts add patterns.
ui.a11y.s7: each has a one-sentence summary for screen readers and a "Show as table" version.
ui.a11y.s8: landmarks (header, navigation, main, complementary), one page heading, labelled controls, alt text on images, and polite announcements for loading and results.
ui.a11y.s9: main controls are at least 48 px.
ui.a11y.t1: Automated: axe-core runs against the Pick and Now screens for Colusa on every change (serious and critical violations fail the check).
ui.a11y.t2: Keyboard walkthrough of the steps, panels, map buttons and dialogs at 1440 and 390 px wide.
ui.a11y.t3: Visual checks of Outdoor mode, and of the pages with colour removed.
ui.a11y.t4: Not yet tested with a panel of people who use assistive technology every day. If something does not work for you, tell us and we will fix it.

ui.gl.bare.text: Days the satellites see bare ground: greenness below 0.2 and no standing water. Bare soil in heavy rain loses topsoil; bare soil in heat dries out and crusts.
ui.gl.et.text: The water a crop pulls from the soil and gives off through its leaves, plus what evaporates from the ground. It is what irrigation and rain have to replace. Measured in inches, or acre-feet per acre (1 acre-foot per acre = 12 inches).
ui.gl.frost.text: Nights when the air near the ground drops to 32 °F or lower at the weather stations near the field. Low spots in a field can be a few degrees colder than the station.
ui.gl.greenness.text: How green the field looks from a satellite, on a 0 to 1 scale. Bare soil is below 0.2, a young or thin crop 0.2 to 0.35, and a full green canopy above 0.6. Standing water reads near 0.
ui.gl.heat.text: Days when the weather stations near the field reach 104 °F or more. Above that, most crops close their leaves and stop growing, and bare soil bakes.
ui.gl.opera.text: NASA’s OPERA product marks every 100 ft square that holds open or shallow water in each clear Landsat or Sentinel-2 image. It sees winter flooding that a greenness reading can miss.
ui.gl.ruleMl.text: The rule calls a field bare below greenness 0.2 and flooded when the water index is high. The machine-learning version learns the same classes from neighbouring fields. We show both and say how often each was right in 2022, a year neither trained on.
ui.gl.soilAnomaly.text: Whether the top few feet of soil hold more or less water than usual for this time of year, ranked against the same dates in other years. 50 is a normal year; 90 means wetter than 9 years in 10. One reading covers several miles, not your field alone.
ui.gl.stress.text: Growing-season weeks when the crop was greener than nothing but under strain: unusual heat, very thirsty air, or weaker growth than in its other years. Two statistical methods look for them; a week counts when either flags it.
ui.gl.waterBalance.text: Crop water use minus the rain that soaks in and stays in the root zone. What is left is the irrigation the crop needs, before losses in the ditch or the system.
